topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series and outlines the core learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: genetic predisposition, bad luck, and environmental epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational drivers of cancer, focusing on the interplay between inherited predisposition, stochastic cellular mutations, and environmental exposures identified through epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Oncogenic pathogens and infectious drivers of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents and pathogens contribute to malignant transformation, exemplified by the etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how direct and metabolically activated chemical and physical carcinogens cause DNA damage and adduct formation.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, microenvironmental factors, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the two-stage model of carcinogenesis, focusing on non-mutagenic tumour promotion, inflammatory microenvironments, and developmental windows of susceptibility.

topics.label: Methods for detecting carcinogens and assessing cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to identify carcinogens and evaluate their risks.

topics.label: Conclusion and closing remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with final framing remarks and a closing summary.
